tldr: The authors propose iTool, an iterative reinforced fine-tuning strategy that combines MCTS-based path exploration with SimPO preference optimization to address the decay of training gains when scaling synthetic tool-use data, achieving ~13% improvement over the base LLaMA3.1-8B model.
contributions: Diagnosis that training gains significantly decay as synthetic tool-use data scales, with limitations manifesting as fragment-level parameter errors (parameter name/value mismatches)
An easy-to-hard warm-up SFT strategy that divides data into easy/medium/hard subsets for curriculum-based learning
An iterative reinforced fine-tuning method (iTool) using step-wise MCTS to explore response diversity and collect fine-grained preference pairs for targeted deficiency correction
Demonstrating that an 8B model outperforms larger open-source and closed-source models on tool-use benchmarks
methods: The method consists of two stages: (1) Warm-up training uses an easy-to-hard curriculum SFT, dividing the ToolACE dataset into three subsets and sequentially fine-tuning the LLM on each. (2) Iterative Reinforcement Learning refreshes a replay buffer by sampling the top 10% highest-perplexity (complex) samples, then applies step-wise MCTS with PUCT to explore response paths and collect preference pairs based on action values Q. SimPO (a reference-model-free variant of DPO) is used for preference optimization, and the process iterates. Parameter-efficient training uses LoRA for SFT and QLoRA for reinforcement learning.
results: iTool-8B achieves 63.26 overall accuracy on BFCL v3, outperforming the base LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct (50.15) by ~13%. It scores 88.82 on Non-live, 78.29 on Live (complex), and 23.84 on Multi-turn. It improves 6.5% over SFT baseline in complex scenarios and outperforms larger models including GPT-4-series and xLAM-8x22b-r (by 5.27 points). On API-Bank, iTool-8B achieves 78.89 overall accuracy and 52.87 on L2. Ablation shows warm-up SFT contributes +2.3 points and IRL contributes +4.2 points on Multi-turn respectively.
limitations: Parameter errors (name/value mismatches) constitute only a small fragment of responses while the majority remains consistent with ground truth, making targeted correction challenging
Training gains decay significantly after ~30% of synthetic data is used under standard SFT
The approach's effectiveness in even more complex or out-of-distribution tool-use scenarios is not thoroughly evaluated
